_meta.purpose: WorkoutSession: the single truth of the in-progress session — its ordered exercise slots (planned / substituted / inserted), each slot's status and set tally, and the DERIVED cursor (current = first pending). This names and versions the shape that lives today on the client as src/app/activeSession.js ({ exercises: [{ name, liftCode, status, source }] } with a derived cursor); the server sees only StateSnapshot.log_history. Read-only, pure; NOT yet wired. Phase 4 makes the live route consume it and enforces the session-priority invariant (findings H-08, H-18).
_meta.cursor_note: The cursor is DERIVED, never stored: currentSlot(session) = the first slot with status 'pending' (mirrors src/app/activeSession.js currentExercise/nextUp so the composer and next-up router can never disagree). This module is the single owner of session-truth selectors (Drift Guard 2: 'session-truth selectors outside WorkoutSession' is banned once wired).
_meta.duplicate_slots_note: Duplicate slot names are ALLOWED and stay independent (F10) — two 'Bench Press' slots are two distinct slots; there is deliberately no name-uniqueness constraint.
_meta.enum_origin: slot_statuses and slot_sources mirror src/app/activeSession.js (STATUS + the 'planned'|'substituted'|'inserted' source strings). activeSession is an ESM client module (not node-requireable), so this contract owns the enums and documents the origin.
_meta.adapter_note: The live client model uses `{ exercises: [{ name, liftCode, ... }] }` (camelCase, no set tallies) while the canonical shape uses `{ slots: [{ name, lift_code, sets_logged, sets_target, ... }] }`. services/workoutSession.js::fromActiveSession() is the single boundary conversion (liftCode→lift_code; sets_logged→0, sets_target→null) Phase 4 uses when the route consumes the client session; it is tested to produce a valid WorkoutSession.
